what: Leveraging a single genotype or LD matrix across multiple phenotypes or summary statistics
title: ColocBoost Tutorial (Advanced Usage)
text: large-scale genetic studies, particularly involving colocalization analysis gene expression across different tissues cell types (GTEx ROSMAP), common encounter scenarios single genotype matrix applies multiple phenotypes. Similarly, summary statistics analyses involving multiple complex diseases (like UK Biobank), researchers often use single LD matrix across various datasets. Traditional methods/usage require duplicating matrices phenotype summary statistics increase computational load also significantly waste memory resources. address inefficiencies, ColocBoost offers streamlined option supports using single genotype matrix alongside matrix phenotypes single LD matrix list summary statistics dataframes. approach leverages consistency across genetic structures reduce redundancy enhance computational efficiency. Example using individual-level data Consider scenario phenotypes share genotype matrix, demonstrated Ind_5traits dataset. Instead loading multiple copies genotype matrix, use first genotype matrix phenotypes covert list phenotype single matrix. Example using summary statistics summary statistics, similar optimization applied using Sumstat_5traits dataset statistical summaries share LD matrix. Example combining individual-level data summary statistics Consider scenario several individual-level phenotypes share common genotype matrix, multiple summary statistics share LD matrix. goal identify colocalization across mixture individual-level phenotypes multiple summary statistics.
code: data("Ind_5traits") X <- Ind_5traits$X[[1]] Y <- do.call(cbind, Ind_5traits$Y) res <- colocboost(X = X, Y = Y) #> Starting checking the input data. #> Starting gradient boosting algorithm. #> Boosting iterations for outcome 4 converge after 34 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 5 converge after 43 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 1 converge after 46 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 2 converge after 67 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 3 converge after 68 iterations! #> Starting assemble analyses and results summary. res$summary_table #> NULL data("Sumstat_5traits") sumstat <- Sumstat_5traits$sumstat LD <- Sumstat_5traits$LD res <- colocboost(sumstat = sumstat, LD = LD) #> Starting checking the input data. #> Starting gradient boosting algorithm. #> Boosting iterations for outcome 4 converge after 34 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 5 converge after 43 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 1 converge after 46 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 2 converge after 67 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 3 converge after 68 iterations! #> Starting assemble analyses and results summary. res$summary_table #> NULL data("Ind_5traits") X <- Ind_5traits$X[[1]] Y <- do.call(cbind, Ind_5traits$Y[1:3]) data("Sumstat_5traits") sumstat <- Sumstat_5traits$sumstat[4:5] LD <- Sumstat_5traits$LD res <- colocboost(X = X, Y = Y, sumstat = sumstat, LD = LD) #> Starting checking the input data. #> Starting gradient boosting algorithm. #> Boosting iterations for outcome 4 converge after 34 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 5 converge after 43 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 1 converge after 46 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 2 converge after 67 iterations! #> Boosting iterations for outcome 3 converge after 68 iterations! #> Starting assemble analyses and results summary. res$summary_table #> NULL
